title: A New Course
sentences: I live in a little old house down by the river.
Some days the power is off, but the house is my own.
This fall I started a course at the school.
On the first day, I asked a man at the power station where the school was.
He pointed to number 4 on the map, between the farm and the factory.
I went through the field, and there it was.
In the course, we talk about the news.
The people in the course come from many places, such as the city.
Both of the people I study with help me with the words I don't know.
Today the mayor came to meet us.
Before I leave, I put my new words on a list.
I think this town is a great place to live.

title: Free Time
sentences: My family came to this town from another country.
Life here is very different from life in our old city.
In my free time, I read a book by the river.
For me, the river is the best part of the town.
My children play in the big field by the school, and they always come home late.
One day a week, a woman at the station asks me questions about my country.
She has a great interest in the world.
She asks why we came here and what we did in our old country.
I also like to hear about her family.
She wants to become a worker at the new factory.
There is always something new to do here, and I have never had so much free time.

title: A Small Business
sentences: This month, my friend and I moved to the town to start a business.
We live in a little house on a high hill, with farms all around it.
Every day we leave home early and go down to our office by the station.
We bring food from the farms to the people of the town.
The office is open all day, and each worker has a job.
A small group of workers helps us.
Few people in town have a truck, so they need us.
While we work, we talk about the news.
My friend says we must keep some money for the winter.
Let me tell you what I think: our business might be small, but it is important to the town.

title: At the Market
sentences: This spring, the town began a new market by the river.
The government set a goal for it: good food from the farms for every home.
I love the market, and I go there every week.
You can buy many kinds of food there.
To get there, follow the river down the hill and turn at the old factory.
The children run to the river while we buy food.
I always have a list in my hand.
The market seems small, but the fact is, it has a lot of food.
The office by the market has information about each farm.
The pay for each worker includes some food.
The mayor is away this week, but the workers know the plan.
What will happen in the winter?
Some people believe the market will close.
In that case, we will buy food at the farms.

title: Study Night
sentences: My kids have a big test at school tomorrow, so we studied at home last night.
They have to remember a lot of words, about half the book.
One of them knows most of the words, but the other one isn't quite ready.
After an hour, the other one asked if it was okay to stop for a bit.
I said yes, and I asked if she needed anything else.
She wasn't sure, so we just talked.
After that, we got all our stuff and started again.
It was sort of late when we stopped, but the kids said thank you.
At the end of the night, I asked if they were ready, and they both said yeah.
It was actually a nice night.
They'll probably do well tomorrow.
Maybe they'll even like the test.

title: A Bad Morning
sentences: This morning, there was a problem with my car.
I don't understand cars, so I asked somebody for help.
A student from the school came, and we looked at the car together.
She was pretty sure it was a small issue.
I had to sit and wait for a minute.
Then she had an idea, but it was hard to do.
I was late to the office, so I said sorry.
I didn't have enough money for a new car, though.
On the way home, I went to the market, where you can buy food by the pound.
The student came back at night, and the car is okay now.
Anyway, I guess everything is good now.
It was a bad morning, but not a bad day.
